The points depend on values in the config file, which is not visible here.
Missing stats are treated as zero rather than reported.

terms.meaning: A player's stats for one match, such as runs and wickets.
A hit to the edge of the field for four or six runs.
A bonus for a bowler taking many wickets in one match.
A bonus for a batter reaching a set score, such as 50 runs.
A number the points are multiplied by, such as double for a captain.

sections.name: File setup, StatLine
sections.title: Config import and stat line shape
sections.what: Loads the scoring rules from one config file and defines the six stats kept for each player in a match.
sections.why: One config file keeps the scoring rules in a single place.
sections.watch_out: The scores depend entirely on the config file, which this code cannot check.

sections.name: Armband, KEYS
sections.title: Captain marks and stat list
sections.what: Defines the three captain states and the list of six stat names, and reads the rules version from the config.
sections.why: The version is kept so each result can show which rules produced it.
sections.watch_out: A new stat must be added here and in the config, or it will be ignored.

sections.name: parseStatLine
sections.title: Cleaning incoming stat data
sections.what: Turns unknown input into a stat line with whole numbers. Returns nothing if the input is not an object, or if any stat is not a non-negative number.
sections.why: Likely reason: bad data is refused before any points are calculated.
sections.watch_out: A missing stat is counted as zero, so a dropped field scores as if the player did nothing.

sections.name: basePoints
sections.title: Points before captain bonus
sections.what: Adds points for each run, boundary, six, wicket, catch and run out. Adds one milestone bonus for the highest run tier reached and one haul bonus for the highest wicket tier reached.
sections.why: Likely reason: tiers do not stack, so only the highest counts.
sections.watch_out: A new tier needs its own branch, or it will never be awarded.

sections.name: playerPoints
sections.title: Final points with captain bonus
sections.what: Multiplies the base points for a captain or vice-captain, and returns the base points for everyone else.
sections.why: The captain bonus is applied last, so it multiplies all points.
sections.watch_out: The result can be a decimal, and nothing here rounds it, so the caller must decide how to display it.

summary: Works out fantasy points for a player from their match stats, with the captain and vice-captain bonuses.
purpose: It turns real cricket stats into the points a fantasy team earns, so scores come from real stat lines only.
why: Likely reason: one versioned rules file keeps scores reproducible and lets each result say which rules were used.
how: It loads the rules from one config file and defines the six stats. It cleans incoming stat data, adds points for each stat, adds the highest milestone and haul bonus reached, then applies the captain or vice-captain multiplier.
inputs: A stat line with runs, fours, sixes, wickets, catches and run outs, plus the captain status of the player.
outputs: A clean stat line, or nothing if the data is invalid. Base points and final points as numbers.
risks: A missing stat counts as zero, so a dropped field looks like no performance. Changing the config changes every new score.
debug: If points look wrong, check the stat values, then the matching rule in the config file. If a stat line is refused, check for negative or non-number values.
